summary: Robert S. Nelson is a historian and archaeologist who studied at Rice University (~1965–1969) and New York University (~1969–1978). He served as a professor at the University of Chicago (~1974–2005) and held a post at Yale University (~2005).

Robert S. P. Beekes was a linguist and Indologist who studied at Leiden University (~1956–1969), completing his doctorate under F. B. J. Kuiper. He held posts at Marnix Gymnasium and Leiden University (1973 and 1979).
Robert Sewell was an Indologist, historian, and archaeologist. He served in the Indian Civil Service (~1868–1894) and held a post as Keeper at the Tamil Nadu Archives.
Robert Seymour Conway was a linguist who studied at the City of London School (~1878–1883). He later held posts at Newnham College (~1887–1893) and Gonville and Caius College (~1888–1894).

Robert Warren Clark is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under adviser and teacher K. L. Seshagiri Rao and completed his doctoral studies under Karen Christina Lang (attested 1994).

Robert Zimmermann was an Indologist who studied at St Beuno's Jesuit Spirituality Centre (~1903–1907) and Humboldt University of Berlin (1908–1913). He served as professor at St. Xavier's College, Mumbai (1914–1930) and led the Bhandarkar Oriental Research Institute.

Robin Coningham is an archaeologist and Indologist who studied at King's College, Cambridge, and completed his PhD under Frank Raymond Allchin (~1989–1994). He held professorships at the University of Bradford (1994–2005) and Durham University (2005).
Robin D. S. Yates is a scholar in sinology and history/archaeology. He completed his PhD at Harvard University (~1975–1980) and held a James McGill Professorship at McGill University (~2002).

Robin Dunbar studied at Magdalen College School, Magdalen College (~1966–1969), and completed his doctorate under John Crook (~1969–1974). He held an academic post at University College London (~1987–1994).

Roderick M. Chisholm was a philosopher who studied at Brown (1934–1938) and Harvard (~1938–1942). He held posts at the Barnes Foundation (~1946), Brown (~1947–1987), University of Graz (1974), and University of Massachusetts Amherst.
Roderick S. Bucknell is a scholar of Buddhist and religious studies. He held a post at the University of Queensland (~1976–2002), where he was attested as an associate professor from 1999 to 2000.
Roger Brown was a scholar of linguistics who studied at the University of Michigan (~1945–1952). He later held an academic post at Harvard University from 1962 to 1994.
Roger Heim studied at École Centrale Paris (~1920–1923) and the Science Faculty of Paris (until 1931). He held a post at the Muséum national d'histoire naturelle from ~1933 to 1970.

Roger R. Jackson is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied at Wesleyan University and completed his PhD at UW–Madison under Geshe Lhundub Sopa, later serving as Associate Professor of Religion at Carleton College (~1989–2016).

Roger T. Ames is a philosopher and sinologist who earned his PhD at SOAS under D. C. Lau. He served extensively at the University of Hawaiʻi (~1978–2016) and held visiting and Fulbright professorships at CUHK, NUS, Peking, and Wuhan.

Roland Barthes was a philosopher and linguist who studied at the Faculty of Arts of Paris and under Émile Benveniste. He held posts at the CNRS (~1952–1959), EHESS (~1962–1976), and the Collège de France (1976–1980).
Roland Steiner is a scholar of Indology and Tibetology who studied under Michael Hahn (attested 1990). He held an assistant professorship at the University of Marburg (attested 2002).

Historian Roland Wenzlhuemer earned degrees at the University of Salzburg and Heidelberg University. He held positions at ZMO (~2003–2005), Humboldt University (~2005–2008), Heidelberg University (2008, 2014), Basel (2013–2014), and became professor at the University of Munich in 2017.

Rolf A. Stein was a Tibetologist and sinologist who studied at INALCO and EPHE under scholars including Pelliot, Maspero, and Demiéville. He served at INALCO (1949–1951), EPHE (1951–1975), and the Collège de France (1965–1982).

Rolf Scheuermann is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned a Magister der Philosophie at the University of Vienna (attested 2010) under Helmut Tauscher, and also studied under traditional teacher Khenpo Chödrag Tenphel.
